findings.title: Exported symbols are not re-exported from the new entry point
findings.body: The new entry point `src/index.ts` only re-exports everything from `./react` and the default export from `./react`, but the old file previously exported types and values directly from `./vanilla` and `react` internals. This breaks downstream consumers that relied on those symbols being available at the top level.

findings.title: Deprecated API usage remains in the new entry point
findings.body: The new entry point `src/index.ts` still exports the deprecated `UseStore` type and the deprecated iterator pattern on `useStore`. These should be removed to align with the new structure and avoid confusion.

findings.title: Deprecated iterator pattern is copied to the new file
findings.body: The deprecated iterator pattern on `useStore[Symbol.iterator]` is copied from the old file to `src/react.ts`. This pattern is slated for removal in v4 and should not be present in new code.

findings.title: Function rename breaks existing imports
findings.body: The function `create` in `src/vanilla.ts` was renamed to `createStore`, but this breaks any existing imports or usages of `create` from this module. The old name should be preserved as an alias or the rename should be coordinated with a major version bump.

summary.problem: The refactor introduces breaking changes by removing and renaming exports, which will break downstream consumers and violate semantic versioning.
summary.done_well: The codebase was successfully split into separate modules (`vanilla.ts`, `react.ts`) following the intended architecture. TypeScript types and internal logic are preserved.
